attacksRun.attack: this v1 repeats the emptiness defect I charged on the G16 and G19 input corpora (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: I tested for it directly, since two sibling input-corpus v1 files in this same chain were REJECTED for records called initial states that contained only the class name. This one does not have that defect. It carries 23 states with substantive per-state content — 16 named protocol frames split by direction, 5 named provider-facing limbs, and 2 lifetime states carrying the actual constraint text (workersPerDistinctKey = 1, reuseAcrossExecutionIds = false, retainAfterTerminal = false, residentWorker = false; and the Cancel-once/cleanup-grace/terminate-if-needed/scratch-removed variant). attacksRun.attack: frameEnvelope, frameIntegrity, and the D-002 platform axis are not carried (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: Live EV-1 says golden traces exercise the frame sets 'plus frameEnvelope (protocolMajor uint64 exactly 1) and frameIntegrity', and both EV-1 and EV-2 scope records 'per D-002 platform'. The subject names neither frameEnvelope nor frameIntegrity as a state and carries no platform field. I decline to charge it: nothing false is asserted, because whatIsAuthored enumerates precisely what is named — seven host frames, nine worker frames, five limbs, and the lifetime plus cancellation variant — and claims no exhaustiveness; and declining frameEnvelope is arguably the prudent reading, since naming it would drag 'protocolMajor uint64 exactly 1' toward being an authored value. Recorded so a later fixture-authoring cycle carries the envelope, integrity, and platform axes forward.

observationsNotFindings: frameEnvelope, frameIntegrity, and the per-D-002-platform scoping present in live EV-1/EV-2 are not materialised as states or fields. Nothing false is asserted and declining frameEnvelope avoids dragging 'protocolMajor uint64 exactly 1' toward an authored value, but a later fixture-authoring cycle must carry these axes forward.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: ACCEPT. 18 attacks run, 17 refuted, 1 not sustained as a finding. 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. All 23 named states trace to live G10 v1 exactByteIntent, and all three enumerations are ORDERED-EQUAL to live: 7/7 closedHostToWorkerFrames, 9/9 closedWorkerToHostFrames, 5/5 consumed provider-facing limbs. Two structural traps were checked before anything was charged: exactByteIntent does not sit under namedCorpusClasses in this harness but on retainedEvidence, and the source fields cite EV-1/EV-2 — I confirmed both are genuine retainedEvidence ids in the live bytes, so the citations are accurate rather than fabricated. The D9 trap is cleanly avoided: none of the five delivery.v2 spellings, no 130, no exit number, no HostTermination, and the only bare integers are 1, 4, and 26. No selector and no R-1 recipe — the apparent 9 'R-1' hits are 7 'DR-102' substrings plus 2 negations. DR-102's live SATISFIED standing is preserved, never reopened and never re-satisfied. Unlike the G16 and G19 input-corpus v1 files I rejected in this chain, this v1 carries substantive per-state content and does not repeat that defect. All cited digests recomputed clean; HEAD 5d5d778; required-now 26.
